newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Former Ivory Coast army chief faces coup tribunal.
newsitem.headline: Former Ivory Coast army chief faces coup tribunal.

text.p: Former Ivory Coast army chief General Robert Guei is to face a military tribunal after being implicated in a 1995 plot to topple the government, the defence ministry said on Monday.

"It was an attempt to destabilise the republican institutions," said a defence ministry statement in the first official admission of a widely reported coup attempt and subsequent arrest of suspected perpetrators.

The statement read on state television said six senior officers and a non-commissioned officer had been dismissed from the service for their part in the coup attempt, which was timed for the eve of presidential elections on October 22, 1995.
A number of officers had been suspended.
Those implicated would be put on trial according to military law, said the statement, adding that their roles were discoverd in an investigation by police and other security agencies.

"As the sanctioned officers had seriously implicated General Robert Guei, chief of army staff, in the conception and preparation of the aborted plot...it has been decided that an inquiry commission be set up, with its composition taking account of his rank, to hear his case," the statement said.
Guei was army chief of staff during the runup to election, won by President Henri Konan Bedie, who first came to power after the death in December 1993 of founding president Felix Houphouet-Boigny.
Guei was removed from his post on the eve of the election, which was marred by violence.
Newspapers reported that Guei had refused to deploy the army to deal with electoral violence linked to an opposition plan to disrupt the elections in protest at a new electoral law.

The government never commented on widespread reports at the time that Guei had been placed under house arrest, but an army inquiry later confirmed there had been a plot. It did not state the nature of the plot or publicly name perpetrators.
Guei has maintained a low profile since he was first assigned to head a youth development scheme and then appointed sports minister until he ws sacked last August.
